extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for DFG individual funding programmes (grant applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the DFG's three-stage decision process (review, assessment, decision) for individual funding proposals, including formal submission checks, peer review, comparative board assessment, committee decision, and notification. Intended to help applicants understand how proposals are evaluated and decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition principle — fund the most promising projects
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on whether to fund a research project is based on the principle of competition: the DFG only funds the most promising projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand proposals are evaluated relative to other submissions; average funding rate is about 30 percent (see Key Figures Portal). The three-stage process is designed to ensure fair comparison. Emphasises comparative merit as the core evaluative standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal submission and requirements check
rubrics_metrics.description: Your proposal is submitted to the DFG Head Office via the electronic platform elan. The first step here is a check to make sure all formal requirements have been met and the submission of the proposal has been correctly carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At this stage the Head Office checks correct subject area allocation and may issue queries. You will receive written confirmation of receipt (including queries if necessary) and information on which Head Office staff are processing your proposal. Ensure all formal requirements and submission procedures on elan are followed to avoid delays or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct subject area allocation / interdisciplinary handling
rubrics_metrics.description: A check is carried out to see whether it was submitted in the correct subject area or if it might be better suited to comparative assessment in a different subject area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting you select the appropriate primary subject area from the DFG subject area structure; you can optionally select additional subject areas. The process is flexible and involves multiple stages to ensure fair competition for interdisciplinary proposals. Choose allocations carefully to ensure the proposal is assessed by the appropriate reviewers/board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of qualified reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The DFG Head Office selects reviewers with the necessary subject-specific qualifications to assess your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are chosen with attention to subject expertise and bias avoidance; researchers from all over the world are asked to provide reviews. Consult the 'General Guidelines for Reviews' and any programme-specific 'Guidelines for the Review' for what reviewers consider important. The reviewers’ vote provides the basis for the subsequent funding decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias mitigation and reviewer confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Special care is taken to rule out bias. Reviewers’ names remain confidential to ensure reviews are comprehensive and transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about Mitigating Bias is available (link provided). Anonymity of reviewers is used to promote frank assessment; any queries about reviews can be clarified via the Head Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality focuses on reviewers' arguments and votes
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewers’ vote provides the basis for the subsequent funding decision. The review board takes into account the reviewers’ comments and the relevance of their arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of the review hinges not just on a vote but on the substance and relevance of reviewers' arguments. Applicants should consult the General Guidelines for Reviews to understand expectations and how reviewers evaluate proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative evaluation by elected review boards
rubrics_metrics.description: After the review stage, the reviews and the proposal itself are submitted to a review board. The review board’s task is to undertake a comparative evaluation of all proposals presented within its subject area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review boards are composed of scientists elected by the community. They prioritise proposals based on comparative merits, reviewers' comments, and the relevance of those arguments. Because assessment is comparative, a strong absolute score may still lose out if other proposals are ranked higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritisation constrained by available funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are prioritised based on the financial resources available and an approval or rejection recommendation is prepared for each proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget constraints can cause review board recommendations to differ from individual reviewers’ votes. Applicants should be aware that funding decisions depend on both scientific ranking and available funds in the subject area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final interdisciplinary decision by the Joint Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommendations put forward by the review boards are submitted to the Joint Committee of the DFG. Based on an interdisciplinary comparison, this body makes the final decision on approval or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Joint Committee conducts an interdisciplinary comparison across subject areas before making final funding decisions; this can affect proposals at the interface of fields. Expect cross-field considerations at the final decision stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and documentation of the decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the decision is made, you will receive written notification from the DFG Head Office. The letter of approval or rejection is also accompanied by all reviews (in anonymised form) as well as notes from the deliberations in the committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receive anonymised reviews and committee deliberation notes with the decision letter. Use this feedback to understand strengths/weaknesses and to inform revisions for future submissions or appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing timeline and status tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: In the area of individual funding, the process from proposal submission through to the written approval/rejection takes about six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can view the processing status of your proposal online at any time via the Proposal Monitor in elan. Plan project timelines accordingly and expect roughly a six-month decision window for individual funding.
